name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_STATEMENT_BASED_3_Q01 - Major plasma proteins and their physiological roles

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements:

(I) Fibrinogen is a major plasma protein essential for the clotting or coagulation of blood.

(II) Globulins in blood plasma are primarily involved in defense mechanisms of the body.

(III) Albumins are major plasma proteins that play a primary role in maintaining osmotic balance.

Which of the statements given are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of First Proposition
Fibrinogens synthesized by the liver circulate in plasma and are converted into insoluble fibrin meshes to arrest hemorrhage. This proposition is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Second Proposition
Globulins include circulating immunoglobulins (antibodies) that protect the body against infectious agents and pathogens. This proposition is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Third Proposition
Albumins generate colloid osmotic pressure that keeps fluid within the vascular compartment and maintains fluid balance across tissues. This proposition is correct.

Step 4: Conclusion
All three propositions regarding plasma protein functions are factually and physiologically accurate.

Final Answer: All three statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_STATEMENT_BASED_3_Q02 - Morphology and haemoglobin concentration of erythrocytes

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements:

(I) Mature mammalian erythrocytes are biconcave in shape.

(II) Mature human red blood cells possess a large spherical nucleus and mitochondria.

(III) A healthy human adult has an average of 12 to 16 grams of haemoglobin in every 100 mL of blood.

Which of the statements given are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of First Proposition
Mammalian erythrocytes lose their nuclei during erythropoiesis and take on a biconcave disc shape to facilitate rapid gas diffusion. This proposition is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Second Proposition
Mature human red blood cells lack a nucleus, mitochondria, and other organelles to maximize cytoplasmic volume for haemoglobin molecules. This proposition is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Third Proposition
Normal clinical laboratory values establish a healthy haemoglobin level of 12 to 16 g per 100 mL of peripheral blood. This proposition is correct.

Step 4: Conclusion
The first and third propositions are accurate, whereas the second proposition is inaccurate.

Final Answer: The first and third statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_STATEMENT_BASED_3_Q03 - Cellular characteristics and secretion of leucocytes

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements:

(I) Leucocytes are nucleated cells that are relatively lesser in number than erythrocytes.

(II) Neutrophils are the least abundant white blood cells in human peripheral blood.

(III) Basophils secrete histamine, serotonin, and heparin during inflammatory reactions.

Which of the statements given are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of First Proposition
White blood cells retain their nuclei throughout their lifespan and number 6,000 to 8,000 per cubic millimeter, which is far lower than the 5 to 5.5 million red blood cells per cubic millimeter. This proposition is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Second Proposition
Neutrophils are the most abundant white blood cells (60 to 65 per cent of total leucocytes), while basophils are the least abundant (0.5 to 1 per cent). This proposition is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Third Proposition
Basophil granules contain and release vasoactive mediators including histamine, serotonin, and the anticoagulant heparin during inflammatory responses. This proposition is correct.

Step 4: Conclusion
The first and third propositions are accurate, whereas the second proposition is inaccurate.

Final Answer: The first and third statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_STATEMENT_BASED_3_Q04 - Antigens antibodies and transfusion compatibility principles

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements:

(I) ABO grouping is based on the presence or absence of two surface antigens, A and B, on red blood cells.

(II) Blood group O individuals possess natural anti-A and anti-B antibodies in their plasma.

(III) Individuals with blood group AB can donate red blood cells to persons of any other blood group.

Which of the statements given are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of First Proposition
The ABO classification is established by two major surface glycoprotein antigens (A and B) situated on the erythrocyte plasma membrane. This proposition is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Second Proposition
Because group O individuals lack surface antigens A and B on their erythrocytes, their plasma develops both natural anti-A and anti-B antibodies. This proposition is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Third Proposition
Group AB erythrocytes carry both A and B antigens; transfusing them into group A, B, or O recipients leads to antibody-mediated clumping. Group O individuals are universal donors, whereas group AB individuals are universal recipients. This proposition is incorrect.

Step 4: Conclusion
The first and second propositions are accurate, whereas the third proposition is inaccurate.

Final Answer: The first and second statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_STATEMENT_BASED_3_Q05 - Pathogenesis and clinical prophylaxis of erythroblastosis

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements:

(I) Nearly 80 per cent of humans possess the Rh antigen on the surface of their erythrocytes and are Rh positive.

(II) Erythroblastosis foetalis occurs when an Rh-positive mother carries an Rh-negative foetus.

(III) Erythroblastosis foetalis can be avoided by administering anti-Rh antibodies to the mother immediately after delivery of the first child.

Which of the statements given are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of First Proposition
The Rh antigen, homologous to that identified in Rhesus monkeys, is expressed on red blood cells in approximately 80 per cent of human individuals. This proposition is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Second Proposition
Erythroblastosis foetalis develops when an Rh-negative mother carries an Rh-positive foetus, causing maternal sensitization to foetal Rh antigens during parturition. This proposition is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Third Proposition
Sensitization of an Rh-negative mother is prevented by administering exogenous anti-Rh immunoglobulin immediately following the delivery of an Rh-positive child, clearing foetal cells before active maternal immunization occurs. This proposition is correct.

Step 4: Conclusion
The first and third propositions are accurate, whereas the second proposition is inaccurate.

Final Answer: The first and third statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_STATEMENT_BASED_3_Q06 - Enzymatic cascade reactions during blood coagulation

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements:

(I) An inactive plasma substance called prothrombin is converted into active thrombin by thrombokinase.

(II) Thrombin converts inactive soluble fibrinogen in plasma into insoluble fibrin threads.

(III) Calcium ions are completely unnecessary for the conversion of prothrombin to thrombin.

Which of the statements given are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of First Proposition
Tissue trauma triggers the assembly of the thrombokinase enzyme complex, which catalyzes the proteolytic activation of prothrombin into active thrombin. This proposition is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Second Proposition
Active thrombin acts as a serine protease that cleaves soluble fibrinogen into insoluble fibrin monomers that polymerize into a mesh trapping formed elements. This proposition is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Third Proposition
Calcium ions are essential cofactors required for multiple steps in the clotting cascade, including prothrombin conversion and fibrin stabilization. This proposition is incorrect.

Step 4: Conclusion
The first and second propositions are accurate, whereas the third proposition is inaccurate.

Final Answer: The first and second statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_STATEMENT_BASED_3_Q07 - Fluid exchange and transport through lymph

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements:

(I) Interstitial fluid has the same mineral distribution as circulating blood plasma.

(II) Lymph is a red fluid rich in erythrocytes and devoid of lymphocytes.

(III) The lymphatic system collects interstitial fluid and drains it back into the major veins.

Which of the statements given are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of First Proposition
Small water-soluble solutes and electrolytes filter freely across capillary walls, providing interstitial fluid with an electrolyte and mineral profile identical to plasma. This proposition is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Second Proposition
Lymph is a colourless fluid that contains specialized lymphocytes but completely lacks red blood cells and larger plasma proteins. This proposition is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Third Proposition
Lymphatic vessels form an extensive drainage network that retrieves surplus tissue fluid from extracellular spaces and empties it into large subclavian veins. This proposition is correct.

Step 4: Conclusion
The first and third propositions are accurate, whereas the second proposition is inaccurate.

Final Answer: The first and third statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_STATEMENT_BASED_3_Q08 - Chambered hearts and circulation in vertebrates

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements:

(I) Fishes possess a two-chambered heart with an atrium and a ventricle exhibiting single circulation.

(II) Amphibians and reptiles (except crocodiles) possess a three-chambered heart with two atria and a single ventricle.

(III) Crocodiles, birds, and mammals possess a four-chambered heart with two atria and two ventricles.

Which of the statements given are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of First Proposition
In fishes, the heart pumps deoxygenated blood to the gills for gas exchange, which then supplies tissues before returning to the heart in a single circuit. This proposition is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Second Proposition
Amphibian and non-crocodilian reptilian hearts have two separate atria receiving oxygenated and deoxygenated blood, but both chambers empty into a solitary ventricle resulting in incomplete double circulation. This proposition is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Third Proposition
Crocodilians, avian species, and mammals exhibit fully divided ventricular walls that create two completely independent circulatory circuits (pulmonary and systemic). This proposition is correct.

Step 4: Conclusion
All three propositions regarding comparative vertebrate heart anatomy and circulation patterns are accurate.

Final Answer: All three statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_STATEMENT_BASED_3_Q09 - Cardiac valves and unidirectional blood flow

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements:

(I) The opening between the right atrium and the right ventricle is guarded by the tricuspid valve.

(II) The bicuspid or mitral valve guards the opening between the left atrium and the left ventricle.

(III) Semilunar valves allow blood to flow backwards from the aorta into the ventricles during diastole.

Which of the statements given are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of First Proposition
The right atrioventricular aperture is guarded by a valve formed of three muscular cusps known as the tricuspid valve. This proposition is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Second Proposition
The left atrioventricular aperture is guarded by a two-cusped valve termed the bicuspid or mitral valve. This proposition is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Third Proposition
Semilunar valves close tightly during ventricular diastole to prevent any retrograde flow of ejected blood from the aorta and pulmonary artery back into the ventricles. This proposition is incorrect.

Step 4: Conclusion
The first and second propositions are accurate, whereas the third proposition is inaccurate.

Final Answer: The first and second statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_STATEMENT_BASED_3_Q10 - Anatomical organization of cardiac nodal tissue

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements:

(I) The sino-atrial node is situated in the right upper corner of the right atrium.

(II) The atrio-ventricular node is located in the lower left corner of the right atrium close to the atrio-ventricular septum.

(III) Purkinje fibres originate exclusively in the atrial walls to initiate atrial contraction.

Which of the statements given are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of First Proposition
The specialized autoexcitable nodal mass called the sino-atrial node is embedded in the superior lateral wall of the right atrium near the entry of the superior vena cava. This proposition is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Second Proposition
The atrio-ventricular node forms a compact mass situated in the posteroinferior interatrial septum in the right atrium. This proposition is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Third Proposition
Purkinje fibres arise from bundle branch divisions on the interventricular septum and ramify through the ventricular walls to stimulate ventricular contraction, not atrial walls. This proposition is incorrect.

Step 4: Conclusion
The first and second propositions are accurate, whereas the third proposition is inaccurate.

Final Answer: The first and second statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_STATEMENT_BASED_3_Q11 - Hemodynamic phases and acoustic heart sounds

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements:

(I) During joint diastole, blood flows passively from pulmonary veins and vena cava into the ventricles through the atria.

(II) Atrial systole increases the flow of blood into the ventricles by about 30 per cent.

(III) The first heart sound (lub) is associated with the sudden closure of the semilunar valves.

Which of the statements given are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of First Proposition
While all four chambers are relaxed in joint diastole, atrioventricular valves stay open and venous blood enters both ventricles passively. This proposition is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Second Proposition
Synchronous contraction of the atria forces an additional bolus of blood into the ventricles, contributing approximately 30 per cent of end-diastolic ventricular filling. This proposition is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Third Proposition
The first heart sound (lub) is generated by the simultaneous closure of the tricuspid and bicuspid atrioventricular valves during early ventricular systole, whereas semilunar valve closure generates the second sound (dub). This proposition is incorrect.

Step 4: Conclusion
The first and second propositions are accurate, whereas the third proposition is inaccurate.

Final Answer: The first and second statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_STATEMENT_BASED_3_Q12 - Lead attachments and waveforms in electrocardiogram

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements:

(I) In a standard electrocardiogram, a patient is connected with three electrical leads: one to each wrist and one to the left ankle.

(II) The P-wave in an electrocardiogram represents electrical depolarisation of both atria.

(III) The termination of the T-wave in an electrocardiogram marks the end of ventricular systole.

Which of the statements given are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of First Proposition
A standard bipolar limb lead recording employs three physical electrodes attached to the right wrist, left wrist, and left ankle to detect electrical axis changes. This proposition is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Second Proposition
The initial upward deflection (P-wave) reflects the wave of electrical excitation sweeping through the atrial myocardium, stimulating atrial systole. This proposition is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Third Proposition
The T-wave records ventricular repolarisation, and the point where the wave completes its return to baseline indicates the conclusion of mechanical systole. This proposition is correct.

Step 4: Conclusion
All three propositions regarding clinical lead attachment and electrocardiogram wave analysis are accurate.

Final Answer: All three statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_STATEMENT_BASED_3_Q13 - Vascular wall anatomy and portal vein

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements:

(I) Arteries and veins both consist of three layers: tunica intima, tunica media, and tunica externa.

(II) The middle muscular layer, the tunica media, is comparatively thicker in veins than in arteries.

(III) The hepatic portal vein carries blood from the intestine to the liver before it enters systemic circulation.

Which of the statements given are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of First Proposition
Blood vessel walls share a three-layered concentric histology comprising endothelial intima, muscular media, and fibrous externa. This proposition is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Second Proposition
The tunica media of a vein is considerably thinner with less smooth muscle and elastic tissue compared to the robust, pressurized tunica media of an artery. This proposition is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of Third Proposition
The hepatic portal system drains capillary beds of the digestive tract and channels nutrient-rich venous blood directly to liver sinusoids prior to vena caval return. This proposition is correct.

Step 4: Conclusion
The first and third propositions are accurate, whereas the second proposition is inaccurate.

Final Answer: The first and third statements are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_BODY_FLUIDS_AND_CIRCULATION_STATEMENT_BASED_3_Q14 - Autonomic and hormonal moderation of heart

questiontext.text:
Consider the following statements:

(I) Sympathetic neural signals increase the rate of heartbeat, strength of ventricular contraction, and cardiac output.

(II) Parasympathetic neural signals decrease the rate of heartbeat, speed of conduction, and cardiac output.

(III) Adrenal medullary hormones decrease cardiac output to prevent cardiac arrest during stress.

Which of the statements given are correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of First Proposition
Sympathetic postganglionic adrenergic nerves release noradrenaline, accelerating pacemaker firing and increasing myocardial contractility, thereby boosting cardiac output. This proposition is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Second Proposition
Parasympathetic cholinergic signals via the vagus nerve release acetylcholine, which hyperpolarizes the pacemaker, slowing heart rate, reducing conduction velocity, and diminishing cardiac output. This proposition is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Third Proposition
Adrenal medullary catecholamines (adrenaline and noradrenaline) act as positive inotropic and chronotropic agents that increase heart rate and cardiac output during stress. This proposition is incorrect.

Step 4: Conclusion
The first and second propositions are accurate, whereas the third proposition is inaccurate.

Final Answer: The first and second statements are correct.
